content: The fourth edition of the World Health Organization's (WHO) Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality, which incorporates the first and second addenda, builds upon over 60 years of WHO's authoritative guidance on drinking-water quality. This guidance has served as a foundational reference for the development of national regulations and standards aimed at ensuring water safety to protect public health. The latest edition includes significant revisions to clarify and expand on the implementation of its recommendations, particularly in the areas of contextual hazard identification and risk management. These are achieved through the establishment of health-based targets, comprehensive water safety plans spanning from catchment to consumer, and independent surveillance mechanisms. This edition reflects a renewed emphasis on primary prevention and introduces additional guidance on best practices, incorporating updates introduced in the third edition. It also includes new risk assessments for various chemical and microbial hazards, as well as for pesticides used in public health applications. Existing reviews of chemicals and waterborne pathogens have been updated to reflect the latest scientific findings. Furthermore, the chapter addressing radiological aspects of drinking-water quality has undergone a comprehensive update.
